outline.target_audience: High school students and math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Flatlander’s Dilemma (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Dimensional Limitation.' Use the analogy of a 2D square living on a piece of paper who cannot perceive a 3D sphere passing through its world, only a circle that expands and shrinks. Prerequisite: Understanding coordinates (x, y).
sections.example: A 2D ant crawling on a sheet of paper. When a ball touches the paper, the ant only sees a growing and shrinking circular shadow.

sections.title: The Logic of Dimensional Projection (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Define 'Projection' as the reduction of dimension. Explain how a 3D object casts a 2D shadow, and a 4D object (tesseract) would cast a 3D shadow. Use grid-based visualizations to show vertices shifting.
sections.example: A wireframe cube casting a shadow on a wall. By rotating the cube, the shadow changes shape—this represents the 'shift' in perspective across dimensions.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Tesseract (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Introduce the Hypercube (Tesseract). Explain the rule: A 0D point moves to create a 1D line; a 1D line moves to create a 2D square; a 2D square moves to create a 3D cube; a 3D cube moves into the '4th direction' (W-axis) to create a Tesseract.
sections.example: An animation showing a small cube inside a large cube, with connecting lines (extrusions) appearing to stretch and contract as it 'rotates' through 4D space.

sections.title: Solving the Shift: The Unfolding Puzzle (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Apply the concept to a puzzle: How to 'unfold' a 4D tesseract into a 3D cross (the Dalí Cross). Focus on the concept of 'nets' (similar to unfolding a 3D box into a 2D cross pattern).
sections.example: The 'Dali Cross'—showing how 8 cubes can be unfolded into a 3D shape, just like a 6-sided die unfolds into a flat paper cross.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition Check (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize that dimensional shifts are about tracking how geometry 'bleeds' from one dimension to another. Emphasize that we perceive 4D objects through their 3D 'slices'.
sections.example: A device (like an MRI scanner) taking 2D slices of a 3D apple; if we were 2D beings, we would 'reconstruct' the apple by seeing these slices appear sequentially.

storyboard.title: The Flatlander’s Dilemma (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Imagine a square trapped in two dimensions.
It cannot perceive the third dimension above it.
A sphere passing through its world looks circular.
animations: Display 2D flat world on screen with #FFFFFF color.
Show a point moving across the 2D plane.
Animate a 3D object intersecting the 2D plane.

storyboard.title: The Logic of Dimensional Projection (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Projection is reducing a shape's dimension.
animations: Show 3D cube casting a 2D square shadow.
Rotate the cube to show shadow geometry change.
Highlight the mapping of vertices to the 2D plane.

storyboard.title: The Geometry of the Tesseract (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Points make lines, lines make squares.
It rotates through the fourth dimension.
animations: Extrude the cube along a 4th dimension axis.

storyboard.title: Solving the Shift: The Unfolding Puzzle (3:30-4:30)
lecture_lines: How do we unfold a 4D tesseract?
This creates the famous Dalí Cross.
animations: Visualize the Tesseract unfolding into 3D space.
Highlight each of the 8 constituent 3D cubes.
Show how the cubes connect at their faces.

storyboard.title: Conclusion and Intuition Check (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Higher dimensions bleed into our lower space.
Geometry is just perspective across dimensions.
animations: Summarize dimensions as points, lines, squares, cubes, tesseracts.
Flash the Tesseract representation in #00FFFF color.
Display the final intuition summary on screen.
